function: Transformer (LQTN) predicts per-RB CSI parameters (RI, CQI 1-2, PMI) from BS and UE geolocation, replacing UE CSI feedback; MAC matching algorithm is not learned (pp. 5-8).
system: SU-MIMO OFDM downlink, FDD, 5 micro-cell BSs with (6, 1) single-polarization panel, 4 UE antennas, 3.5 GHz (7 GHz in one test), 100 MHz; no RIS (pp. 9-11).
method: Learnable-queries Transformer (1-layer encoder, 2-layer decoder), supervised offline training as multi-output classification of RI, CQI, PMI per RB; one model per BS; retrained per scenario (pp. 5-6, 9).
data_channel: Vienna 5G system-level simulator, channel model 3GPP TR 25.890 (Table II), OpenStreetMap urban micro scenario; 50,000 random geolocations with CSI labels for training, 5,000 for testing (pp. 9-10).
test_conditions: Train 50,000 geolocations (Peng Cheng, 3.5 GHz), test 5,000 new ones plus position-error and speed sweeps; Shopping Mall at 3.5 and 7 GHz only after retraining (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Learned: FCNN, Independent FCNN, Independent Transformer (ablation) for CSI. Non-learned: 5G CLSM with UE CSI feedback (3 ms delay), 5G Round-Robin and Best-CQI schedulers (pp. 9, 12-13).
metrics: Normalized MAE of RI, CQI, PMI prediction; per-user and per-RB throughput; spectral efficiency; Jain's fairness index; parameters, memory, FLOPs and compute time (pp. 9-14).
complexity: Table I: 43,975,233 parameters, 167.8 MB, 3.19 GFLOPs, 5.32e-5 s (estimated from FLOPs) per BS-UE pair over 100 RBs; M3-MAMA scheduler O(W^2) (pp. 8-10).
q1_support: p. 9: "Referring to 3GPP standard, the proposed feedback-free MIMO transmission, multi-BS association and multi-RB allocation are implemented on the Vienna 5G system-level simulator [18]" and "a typical Urban micro (UMi) scenario"; Table II (page 10, read from the page image) lists the channel model as 3GPP TR 25.890, which is not one of the named models (see notes).
q2_support: p. 11: "We therefore retrain all compared models in this new environment" and "The purpose of this experiment is not to claim universal zero-shot generalization"; p. 9: "Another 5,000 randomly generated user geolocations are used as test data" (held-out data of the same scenario). Not met: the new scenario and bands are evaluated only after retraining, and the position-error and speed sweeps are parameter sweeps.
q3_support: p. 9: "we add two additional CSI prediction baselines, namely Fully Connected Neural Networks (FCNN) and Independent FCNN" (learned); p. 11: "the proposed CaFTRA achieves the best prediction performance among all baselines" (normalized MAE); p. 12: "CaFTRA outperforms 5G CLSM by around 20% in terms of per-user throughput" (non-learned 5G CLSM with UE feedback).
q4_support: p. 9: "we also present the corresponding model complexities, including the number of parameters, memory usage, FLOPs, and computational time" and "CaFTRA requires only 44 million parameters and 168 MB of memory" (Table I on page 10: 3,192,893,440 FLOPs); p. 8: "the overall computational complexity is O(W 2 )" for the matching scheduler.
q5_support: p. 9: "a historical CSI dataset with 50,000 randomly sampled user geolocations is first generated in Vienna 5G system-level simulator". Not met: the dataset is generated by the authors, no link or DOI is given, and the only mention of code is p. 9: "The number of parameters and FLOPs can be obtained from the codes", with no link or release statement.
notes: Area 2: the learned Transformer predicts RI, CQI and PMI from geolocation to replace CSI feedback, and its main metric is the normalized MAE of CSI prediction (pp. 5-7, 11); the PMI and CQI outputs touch precoding and link adaptation, and the M3-MAMA matching scheduler (pp. 7-8) is not learned, so the area follows the learned CSI predictor. q1=1 needs confirmation: Table II (page 10, read from the page image because it is not in the extracted text) lists the channel model as 3GPP TR 25.890, not TR 38.901, inside the Vienna 5G system-level simulator with OpenStreetMap urban micro scenarios (p. 9); the reviewer should confirm that this counts as a standardized model. q2=0: the Shopping Mall scenario and the 3.5 and 7 GHz bands are evaluated only after retraining all models (p. 11), the position error (r95) and speed sweeps (Figs. 7, 14) are parameter sweeps, and the paper says it does not claim zero-shot generalization. q3=1: FCNN and Independent FCNN are learned baselines on the same task, and 5G CLSM with UE feedback is the non-learned baseline compared on throughput (pp. 9, 11-12); the Independent Transformer is an ablation and is not counted. q4=1: Table I (page 10, page image) gives parameters, memory, FLOPs and time, but the time is estimated from FLOPs and an H100 peak rate (p. 9) rather than measured. q5=0: the dataset is generated by the authors in the simulator and the only mention of code is 'the codes' without a link (p. 9). Figs. 6-14 and Tables I-II were checked as page images.
